Subject: RFP: data locality follow-up + capacity/sustainability question

Hi Ben —

Thanks again for the briefing yesterday. A couple of clarifications from our legal and infra teams that we want captured in the RFP response:

1) We are asking vendors to confirm whether runtime inference can be guaranteed to execute in a specific legal jurisdiction (EU) for all PII-bearing request payloads, including fallbacks where capacity is constrained. Please indicate whether Redwood offers a contractual "hard residency" (requests never leave EU compute) or a "logical residency" (data is encrypted and only keys in EU).

2) We're also interested in your approach to regional capacity sustainability: can you commit to reserved hot capacity for critical workloads during seasonal spikes, and do you have any sustainability commitments (e.g., renewable energy % mapped by region) that affect placement decisions?

3) Bonus question: we've seen the concept of a 'data passport' — a signed assertion that a set of metadata/IDs for objects remain accessible across regions while the underlying content stays resident. Do you support any mechanism like that (signed location assertions or verifiable audit tokens)?

Please respond with short answers and attach any supporting annexes. We need to circulate vendor responses internally by EOD Wednesday.

Best,
Sarah
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Insurance

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the clear list. High-level responses below; I'll loop in our regional product lead (Marissa) for the annex and technical specifics.

1) Residency model — short answer: Redwood supports both models.
   - Hard residency: for Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) and some Dedicated contracts we can contractually restrict execution to EU-only compute; that is enforced via our private control plane and routing policies.
   - Logical residency: for Hosted API customers we provide strong cryptographic guarantees (BYOK/KMS in-region, TEEs when requested) and routing controls. When capacity forces fallback, requests are only routed to a compatible region if permitted by customer policy; otherwise they queue or failover to Dedicated pools owned by the customer.

2) Regional capacity & sustainability — short answer: reserved hot capacity is available on Dedicated and Dedicated+Burst SKUs. Public-hosted customers can purchase capacity commitments for seasonality. We publish our regional energy mix per region in the sustainability annex; for committed pools we can negotiate higher renewable-mix SLAs.

3) Data passport — short answer: we do not currently implement a "signed location passport" as a standardized token, but we can provide verifiable audit artifacts: signed request/response logs, region-tagged attestations, and time-stamped STS tokens tied to KMS key-ids. We are exploring a small, interoperable signed-metadata feature; Marissa will include the product roadmap note.

I'll attach our playbook sections and the XLS annex that map controls to RFP clauses.

Thanks —
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attached are the requested artifacts:
- Redwood_Regional_Residency_Playbook_v1.3.pdf (section 3.2 addresses hard vs logical residency; section 5 shows routing/fallback policies)
- RFP_Annex_Data_Location.xlsx (row-level mapping to your RFP clauses: residency, KMS, audit stamps, deletion proof)

Short, technical clarifications inline below:

On hard vs logical residency:
- Hosted API: we offer "region pinning" at the API key or tenant level (soft enforce). For strict contractual hard residency we advise Dedicated or Private deployments. We can include contractual clauses that restrict cross-border routing and expose penalty SLAs for violations.

On fallbacks and capacity constraints:
- Policy model: customers choose a fallback policy per route: 1) fail (block), 2) queue with priority, 3) fallback to customer-owned Dedicated pool, 4) fallback to pre-agreed alternate EU region.
- Operational controls: region-aware autoscaling, pre-warmed pools for predictable spikes, and a drain plan for rolling upgrades to avoid warm/cold start spikes.

On observability and verifiability (data passport idea):
- We emit signed audit bundles that include: request id, model variant, region tag, timestamp, and KMS key-id. Each bundle is signed by our control plane and can be used as an evidence artifact in audits.
- Roadmap: we are prototyping a portable signed manifest (think JWT with region claims + signature) for Multi-Cloud portability; ETA for pilot Q1 2027.

Other notes:
- BYOK: supported (AWS KMS/Google Cloud KMS/Azure Key Vault). For Private deployments we support HSMs.
- DSAR / deletion: deletion requests are logged and produce a deletion audit record; we also support retention carve-outs per route.
- Data-in-transit and at-rest: TLS1.3, per-tenant encryption at rest with customer KMS keys on Dedicated/Private.

I've highlighted the exact XLS rows that map to your RFP sections and included suggested contractual language in the playbook appendix. If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute technical deep-dive during your vendor evaluation window.

Regards,
